news.title: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
news.summary: Claude Code is leaking sensitive information on public GitHub instances thanks to a partial oversight in the way its settings files are handled. That's the finding of AI security researchers at Apiiro, who discovered thousands of secrets, including database passwords, API tokens, and root logins, amid Claude Code settings files embedded in GitHub repositories. The leak stems from the way Claude Code handles user approval for automated shell commands. When a user chooses the "Yes, and don't ask again" option to approve running a command, that choice gets stored as part of a rule in the local ".claude/settings.local.json" file on the user's computer. That rule is sometimes coded as a pattern, but the command itself is often written to that settings file as is, including any sensitive information that may be embedded within it. This isn't really a significant security issue if the settings file stays on the user's local machine (assuming that machine doesn't become compromised itself, of course).

news.summary: Simulation, which has long been the proving ground for robots learning to walk, roll and hop, is now helping researchers teach robots tasks that require a finer touch: aligning gears, connecting cables and assembling small components. The shift from locomotion to manipulation is taking center stage at this week’s Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin, Texas, alongside the rise of agentic robotics — a new paradigm that integrates frontier agents to create interpretable code for physical robotics systems. At CoRL, NVIDIA is introducing new open robotics technologies, including world action models, simulation tools, benchmarks and agentic workflows. Two NVIDIA papers are among six finalists out of thousands of submissions for the Best Paper Awards at CoRL: GRAIL (Generating Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from World Models), which presents a digital generation pipeline for 3D assets and simulator-ready scenes for robot learning. RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies, which introduces a robot model and training recipe that scales visuomotor context three orders of magnitude beyond state-of-the-art policies without growing inference latency. These advancements help researchers train robots on complex tasks, evaluate their performance across changing conditions and use failures to guide further learning — building the precision, adaptability and autonomy needed to move from lab demonstrations to industrial deployment.

Girish Rao, vice president of information technology at Lubrizol, says the company is building a digital foundation that connects business processes, modern data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support its research and development (R&D) teams. Their goal is to combine decades of accumulated technical data with the deep expertise of chemists and engineers who understand customer needs as well as the physical constraints of their work. Data scientists can help identify patterns, test new hypotheses, and model possibilities before researchers conduct physical experiments. news.summary: Humans have wondered about life beyond our planet since ancient times, and researchers have worked hard for decades to find any definitive signs, to no avail. Now, researchers at the SETI Institute have turned to a rather interesting approach in their search for intelligent life beyond planet Earth (via: Phys.org). The latest research involves something called game theory, which scientists believe could help them determine when an alien civilization might attempt to contact us. The problem here is that even if someone out there is deliberately sending radio signals towards Earth, there is no guarantee we'd be listening at the right time, or even looking in the right direction. Researchers Isabel Gerrard and Sofia Sheikh believe there might be a way to narrow down those possibilities, and it involves trying to figure out how another intelligent civilization would approach the same problem. For anyone unfamiliar with game theory, it's a mathematical concept concerned with making decisions based on what another person might do.

news.title: AI-assisted learning platform helps robots reason beyond literal commands
news.summary: Humans are intuitive by nature. We can sense meaning beyond the literal words that we encounter. Now, a new artificial intelligence-assisted learning platform developed by MIT engineers is enabling robots to read larger meaning into a human’s natural language commands. In a study to be presented at the annual Conference on Robot Learning this month, researchers from MIT and New York University introduce FLEX, a flexible feature-editing pipeline for robot motion-planning. With FLEX, humans can interact with a robot by giving it instructions in natural, conversational language. The robot can not only follow the instructions literally but also read into the words to draw larger generalizations that help to improve its motion-planning task. news.title: Clearing up a robot’s fuzzy memory
news.summary: In an emergency, a human might someday ask a robotic assistant to fetch a wall-mounted defibrillator located down the hall. But if the robot has incorrectly labeled the defibrillator as a fire extinguisher in its stored memory, it may not know where to find the life-saving device.This robotic assistant could benefit from a new memory system created by MIT researchers. The system identifies entries in a robot’s memory that might be wrong and corrects the descriptions of mislabeled objects. In the future, this method could make household or industrial robots better able to perform complex, multistep tasks, such as clearing a dining room table or working alongside human collaborators to assemble a piece of machinery. Called UQ-DAAAM (which stands for Uncertainty Quantification for Describe Anything, Anywhere, at Any Moment), the system compares multiple descriptions of the same object, seen from different viewpoints, to quantify the robot’s uncertainty about what it saw. It then selects additional views to reduce the uncertainty and combines these captions into a more accurate description of the object, which it saves to memory.The researchers also employed a special technique to streamline this process so a mobile robot can continually update uncertain memory entries in real time. news.title: OpenAI Drops NDAs With Public Officials for Data Center Projects
news.summary: The ChatGPT maker won’t use NDAs with public officials as part of its new data center community commitments. The ChatGPT maker won’t use NDAs with public officials as part of its new data center community commitments. Following this week’s midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion, OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won’t use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials. Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to hide discussions between developers and local officials. However, OpenAI says it is now allowing “only narrow protections covering legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information.” In October, Amazon announced it would no longer use NDAs with government agencies it works with on data center projects. OpenAI’s additional commitments include paying “the full cost” of electricity it uses and the “infrastructure needed to serve us.” It will make opportunities for local communities by publishing the jobs it expects to create and by reporting on hiring.

news.title: Runway Halves GPU Cost for Real-Time 57B Video Model, Now Runs on 4 H100s
news.summary: Every conversation has a rhythm. One person stops talking, the other starts and that back-and-forth pace sets the tone. We interrupt each other, talk over each other and bounce from topic to topic, staying on track the whole time. To be convincing — to cross the uncanny valley — a virtual character has to keep that same rhythm. Runway Characters can turn a single image into a live character you can talk to, and behind it is a roughly 57B-parameter autoregressive video diffusion transformer. At 24 frames per second (fps), that model has to generate a new four-frame chunk of 704x1088 video every 166.7ms, for one user at a time, for as long as the conversation lasts.
